Sports.title: Essex cricket star charged with two counts of rape
Sports.content:
The Essex cricketer Robin Das has been charged with two counts of rape and will appear at London Crown Court on Friday, October 9.

Das, 24, was arrested in August last year following allegations of a woman being raped in Brixton in March 2024.

A spokesman for the Metropolitan Police said: 'Robin Das of Queens Road, Waltham Forest, was charged on 23 July 2026 with two counts of rape.

'The charges follow his arrest on 27 August 2025 following reports of a woman being raped in Brixton on 30 March 2024. The woman continues to be supported by specialist officers.'

Das, predominantly a batsman, made his debut for Essex in 2020 and has gone on to make over 60 appearances for the county in all formats. His only senior game this season was in a One-Day Cup match against Middlesex on July 21.

He has been suspended since being charged two days after that match.

Robin Das has played over 60 games for Essex since making his debut in 2020

Essex CC said in their statement: 'Essex County Cricket Club can confirm that a male member of the playing staff, currently under contract with the club, recently appeared in court in relation to an incident that took place outside club activities.

'Throughout, the club has remained in contact with the ECB, PCA, the Cricket Regulator and the player with regard to the matter, which included an immediate and ongoing suspension. The club will continue to follow all appropriate legal processes and guidance.

'As a club we have strict safeguarding and HR procedures in place, and all employees of Essex County Cricket Club are required to meet the highest standards of professional conduct at all times.

'As legal proceedings are in progress, the club are unable to make any further comment at this time.'

Sports.title: I knocked back Mourinho and shared a pizza with Henry... stepping up to international level doesn't faze me, says well-travelled Binks
Sports.content:
I knocked back Mourinho and shared a pizza with Henry... stepping up to international level doesn't faze me, says well-travelled Binks

Asked to describe the journey which has taken him to the brink of full international recognition with Scotland, Luis Binks smiles and answers with three words. Nice. Weird. Random.

It feels all of that and more. A life less ordinary punctuated by encounters with superstars and the faintly surreal. Where to even begin?

Given he spent his formative years there, Spurs feels apt. Born in Kent, the defender came through the club’s academy but could see the roadblock to the first team up ahead when a professional contract was put in front of him at the age of 17.

Having resolved to turn it down and try his luck elsewhere, he informed the academy staff of his decision.

‘They said: “That’s fine... you can tell that to the first-team manager”,’ he explained.

‘Then (Jose) Mourinho came around with his entourage.’

Binks trains with the Scotland squad for the first time in La Manga

The centre-back has been starring for Danish side Brondby, who he captains

Mourinho tried to convince a young Binks to stay at Spurs, but he moved on

There are probably easier conversations for a teenager to have. Binks, though, admirably stuck to his guns.

‘He said: “You know I gave Raphael Varane his debut and captaincy at 18”, and all this and that,’ Binks added.

‘I was thinking I’m not at Real Madrid and I’m not Varane. If he had the opportunity to buy a centre-back for £50-60 million, he was going to do it. I didn’t want to get stuck in that cycle of being an old player stuck in the 23s.

‘He said: “You’ll come on pre-season, you’ll play the cup games and then you can go on loan if you’re not happy”.

‘I was like, no. I was quite stubborn. I had it in my head. No one was pushing me. It was me. Then he said: “Okay, that’s fine”. And I think a couple of weeks after I left, he got the sack anyway.’

It wasn’t a decision that he took without a safety net. Binks shared an agent with Thierry Henry and knew there was an offer to join the newly appointed Montreal Impact manager in Canada and gain the first-team exposure he craved.

It started well with a couple of appearances in front of packed stadiums. Covid then changed everything.

‘It all shut down,’ he recalled. ‘I didn’t go home for nine months. We were training on our own, four players at a training ground at a time on half a pitch, doing keep-up, whatever.’

After leaving Spurs, Binks made his way to Canada, where he played for Montreal Impact

The defender spent time with his Montreal head coach Henry during the Covid lockdown

At least kicking a ball gave him some sense of normality. Away from the training ground, his life was about to get utterly bizarre.

‘I was in another hotel by the airport — it felt like prison,’ Binks said. ‘One day, he (Henry) rang me and said: “I’m in this hotel on my own. Do you want to move in on another floor?”

‘We couldn’t be too close and everything. So, I was like, yeah.

‘So, I moved into the hotel with him and it was just me and him and maybe two staff, a cleaner and a receptionist.

‘It was probably for about two months. Then I got an apartment and things started moving a bit. Those two months were a bit surreal.’

Binks believes the end of the arrangement probably came not a moment too soon.

‘I think I was getting on his nerves a little bit,’ he laughed.

‘But I think it was good because he didn’t have anyone else out there as well. It was just me and him.

‘I’d go for a run in the morning. He’d be sat in the reception and I’d come back and just try and pick his brains — who’s the best manager you worked with, best player you played with, all these things.

‘I’d have dinner in my room, but, one day, he did ring me and said: “Do you want to go and get a pizza?”

‘One of his friends had a pizza shop in Montreal and they shut the restaurant, so it was just me and him having a pizza in it. He was brilliant for me and a good guy.’

The journeyman returned to England to play for Coventry before leaving for Brondby

His sense of adventure heightened by moving abroad, Binks signed for Bologna and was farmed out for a season to Como. His team-mate for that season in Serie B? Try Cesc Fabregas, now manager of the upwardly mobile Italian club.

Little wonder that meeting up with the established stars of the Scotland squad this week hasn’t been quite so daunting.

‘I don’t regret any of the decisions I’ve made because I think it’s grounded me as a player better, experiencing different cultures, different playing styles,’ he reflected.

‘To now be sitting here with some of the Scotland players who have had the careers they’ve had, I’ve always been around people like that.’

The very fact that he now captains Danish side Brondby after moving there last year from Coventry underscores his credentials and fully justifies the quirky career path he’s followed.

Sebastien Pocognoli certainly likes what he sees in him — a vocal, ball-playing centre-back who seems well suited to the aggressive front-foot approach the Belgian advocates.

Despite his English accent and the fact he played in the England youth set-up, Binks is all-in on this.

‘I always enjoyed playing for Scotland,’ he said of a relationship which stretches back to wearing the Dark Blue in the Victory Shield.

‘It felt like a very close-knit group. Then I got called up to both England and Scotland at the same time and I probably got pushed down the England route a bit more.

‘Being in an English academy, there were a few players in my Tottenham team that were going away with England as well.

‘I don’t want to make it sound bad, but when you were with England the boys who were at big clubs, your Chelseas, your Arsenals, your Man Citys, they were doing this, they were doing that.

‘Whereas when you went with Scotland, it was just “we’re all here to play for Scotland. Let’s do as best as we can”.

New Scotland boss Sebastien Pocognoli has named a new-look squad for his first matches

‘I enjoyed being around the boys. It felt like a boys’ holiday, like you were with your mates as opposed to just playing with anyone. I’ve always just enjoyed the whole vibe around the Scotland camp.’

His family’s pride at being brought in ahead of the Nations League campaign is palpable, the Caledonian connection being a maternal grandfather from Dunbar.

‘Even when you sign for a new club you don’t really get this feeling,’ he said of the call-up. ‘I can’t really describe it because to represent the country is every boy’s dream growing up.

‘My family are buzzing. My mum was screaming. She always took us back up there as kids to try and keep that Scottish going in us.

‘I owe that to her because when I was brought up in England, if I hadn’t kept going back to Scotland in the six-week holidays and Easter holidays, then I probably wouldn’t feel that connection.

‘We used to always go up to try and find the Loch Ness Monster and go to Dunbar. We’d go to Parkhead and Ibrox too. We always used to go and see a game as well.’

Those who can make it will be at Hampden next week too, in the hope of seeing him strutting his stuff against Switzerland, the next chapter in a captivating story. The beauty of it is that it’s only really beginning.

Sports.title: PREMIER LEAGUE REPORT CARD - PART ONE: Arsenal begin the defence of their crown, Brighton and Brentford are the surprise standouts and faltering Fulham remain winless - so what grades will they get?
Sports.content:
PREMIER LEAGUE REPORT CARD - PART ONE: Arsenal begin the defence of their crown, Brighton and Brentford are the surprise standouts and faltering Fulham remain winless - so what grades will they get?

The international break is upon us, calling a brief halt to a thrilling new Premier League campaign. The first five weeks have seen a flood of goals, plenty of upsets and many contentious moments.

With that in mind, Daily Mail Sport have compiled report cards for all 20 sides so far. Here are the first ten to go under analysis....

ARSENAL

Position: 2nd. Points: 12

As expected the reigning champions hit the ground running proving early on that they will be hard to dethrone by earning four wins from five.

The Gunners picked up where they left off last season, beginning the campaign with an emphatic 3-0 home win against newly promoted Coventry to set the tone for their first title defence in 22 years.

Since the opening day, Mikel Arteta's men have won a number of extremely testing fixtures. The Gunners claimed three points away at Aston Villa, who have caused them trouble in previous seasons, as well as beating London rivals Chelsea at home and winning at the ever hostile Stadium of Light where big money signing Bruno Guimaraes scored his first goal for the club.

But it has not been a flawless start for Arsenal as they endured a miserable afternoon on the south coast losing 3-0 to Brighton – the first time they have failed to score in a Premier League game since January.

Nevertheless the Gunners still look formidable and are poised to challenge for the title again and perhaps seek the European glory they missed out on in Budapest in May.

Grade: A-

Despite a small blip Arsenal's start indicates they will be tough to dethrone and are after more silverware this time around

ASTON VILLA

Position: 16th. Points: 4

After a standout season last year where they finished fourth and won the Europa League, the Villains have not carried their excellent form from last season into this.

Unai Emery, now in his fifth season at Villa Park, has been unable to get his new-look side to tick yet despite some promising signs. Villa started the season on a whimper losing 4-0 at the hands of Brighton, conceding all four goals in the first 31 minutes of the game.

Since their opening day thrashing, Villa have lost to both Arsenal and midlands rivals Nottingham Forest, while they failed to score against new boys Hull in a bore draw.

Villa can be somewhat excused for a slow start with this season being a slight transition year for the club after losing several key players over the summer including their two top scorers Ollie Watkins and Morgan Rogers as well as star centre-half Ezri Konsa. But even the most pessimistic of supporters would not have envisaged a start such as this.

They did manage to pick up their first three points of the season just before the break in a well-deserved 3-2 victory away at Tottenham and beat Club Brugge away from home in their Champions League opener. Big money signings Nicolas Jackson and Johan Manzambi have also looked to be finding their feet in the side.

After the first five games Villa sit two places from the drop, and will need Emery to mastermind a turnaround in form quickly if this season is to end with more success.

Grade: C-

Unai Emery has worked wonders during his time at Villa Park but how will he manage this transition?

BOURNEMOUTH

Position: 17th. Points: 3

Another side that overperformed last season and have not been able to keep up the pace is Bournemouth, with the Cherries winless under new manager Marco Rose going into the international break.

Bournemouth seem to have suffered the same fate many mid-table sides do when playing in Europe as they won their first ever European bout away at Real Sociedad but are yet to get off the mark in the Premier League.

The South Coast side managed their highest ever finish in English football last season by placing sixth, only three points off the Champions League places, and did very well to hold onto to almost all of their top talents in the summer.

But the Cherries have clearly had one very costly loss with head coach Andoni Iraola upping sticks for Liverpool. His replacement Marco Rose arrived with a glittering resume having coached some of Germany's biggest sides but has yet to realise his vision at the Vitality.

A harsh run of fixtures have made this a tough first month of the season for Bournemouth, having to face Man City, Liverpool and Newcastle already, but there is no excuse for not winning a single game yet and the pressure will be on Rose and his side to deliver when they return.

Grade: D

Bournemouth will have to pick up form quick if they want to avoid a spiral into a relegation scrap

BRENTFORD

Position: 4th. Points: 9

From one extreme to the other Brentford have been marvellous in their opening fixtures as Keith Andrews continues to prove people wrong with his high-octane pressing machine churning out results every week.

As one of five unbeaten teams, the Bees are buzzing with two wins and three draws to kick off the season.

A strong transfer window saw Brentford hold onto key players, including Caoimhin Kelleher and Igor Thiago, and add some excellent young players which has helped create a free-scoring team that looks so hard to beat.

The 3-0 drubbings of Chelsea and Tottenham demonstrated the lethal nature of this Brentford attack, with five of the six total goals coming in one half of each game.

Three score draws in between these two London derbies leaves them in contention for a sustained European push.

Grade: A

Brentford look ready to push to new heights this season after thrashing rivals Chelsea and Spurs at home

BRIGHTON

Position: 3rd. Points: 10

Brighton have enjoyed a dream start to the season with Fabian Hurzeler having orchestrated some truly excellent performances. His free-scoring side have netted a whopping 16 goals in their opening five games, more than any other side in the top flight.

The Seagulls kicked off with a bang beating Aston Villa 4-0 at home and have since enjoyed victories over Coventry and champions Arsenal, keeping clean sheets against both. Hurzeler's men have dropped points to Chelsea and Leeds in-between but were then buoyed by a magnificent Carabao Cup comeback victory over Manchester United.

Brighton as always had an excellent window and it shows, with new boys Malick Yalcouye, Chema Andres and Luka Vuskovic having already impressed. The Seagulls were particularly brilliant in beating Arsenal through a patient defensive approach that forced the champions to play long and lose possession constantly.

Questions will be asked about Brighton's ability to maintain this style of play over the course of 38 games, with the added strain of European football, but their performances have certainly shaken up the Premier League and it will be fascinating to see how their season unfolds.

Grade: A

The Seagulls are flying! Brighton are becoming a dreaded fixture after a blistering, goal heavy start to the season

CHELSEA

Position: 10th. Points: 7

To the surprise of many who tipped Chelsea to be fighting for the title the Blues have been remarkably inconsistent in their opening games.

After another whirlwind summer that saw Chelsea bring in Xabi Alonso as head coach and sign 11 new players, it looked as if they had finally plugged the gaps in their squad and were ready to seriously challenge – especially when playing only one game a week.

The Blues have instead looked as unstable as ever, conceding more goals than any other side so far (12) and picking up one point from their last available nine. It is not all bad news at Stamford Bridge as summer signing Morgan Rogers has looked electric and has become the final piece of a fearsome front three alongside Cole Palmer and Joao Pedro. But the midfield has looked barren without Moises Caicedo and the defence looks calamitous.

It is clear that Alonso intends to outscore opponents this season at the expense of clean sheets but currently his side are just shipping goals and cannot score enough to pick up wins. Chelsea won their opening two matches against Fulham and Brighton in exciting fashion but since have dropped points to Hull and lost London derbies to Arsenal and Brentford.

Sat exactly in the middle of the table, Chelsea are already in danger of another disappointing season unless Alonso can find a balance in his squad and find consistency.

Grade: C-

Free scoring Chelsea will need to sort out their defensive woes if they are to avoid another disappointing season

COVENTRY CITY

Position: 18th Points: 3

The first of the new boys to receive their grade is Frank Lampard's Championship winners Coventry City. After a 25-year absence from the Premier League the Sky Blues will have one objective for this season: survival.

Anticipation for Coventry's first Premier League season in over two and a half decades was sky high in the summer but their start has been woeful.

The new boys tasted defeat in their first four games without scoring. Lampard struggled to bring in proven Premier League talent over the summer and it has shown in his team's performances.

They were handed some unfortunate early fixtures having to play both Arsenal and Manchester City in their first three games, but losing at home to Hull in-between those two games is a real cause for concern. Brighton's 5-0 demolition at the Building Society Arena has left some believing Coventry are condemned within the first month.

They managed to breathe some life into their survival hopes at midlands rivals Nottingham Forest with an impressive 1-0 victory thanks to a beautiful Jay DaSilva goal but they will need a lot more if they are to get out and stay out of the bottom three.

Grade: C-

Lampard got Coventry into the top flight but this will be the Premier League legend's biggest test yet

CRYSTAL PALACE

Position: 15th. Points: 4

For some Palace fans the international break will come as a welcome respite after a hectic summer and stressful start to the season.

A new manager, new defence and new beginnings in the Europa League promised a chaotic season and it has delivered so far. One win in five is cause for concern but Eagles fans must be patient and allow the squad to adapt to new manager Pierre Sage's system.

Similarly to their west London rivals Chelsea, Palace have had no problem scoring but are struggling to keep opposing teams out at the other end, conceding 11 goals already. A loss to newly promoted Ipswich has prompted suggestions the Eagles could slip into a relegation scrap if they are not careful.

The Europa League has provided a welcome distraction and their hope for back-to-back European trophies was inflated by a rampant 4-0 win over Lech Poznan in their opener.

All in all Palace seem to be par for the course, their form suggests a slight but not urgent worry for relegation and an exciting opportunity in the Europa League where they have nothing to lose but everything to gain.

Grade: C+

Crystal Palace have been free scoring at one end but unable to keep opponents out at the other

EVERTON

Position: 7th. Points: 9

After a disappointing end to their first season at the eye-catching Hill Dickinson Stadium veteran boss David Moyes has the Toffees looking sweet again.

Everton remain unbeaten and look solid all over the pitch. Thierno Barry seems to finally be coming good, Dewsbury-Hall has built on last season's impressive showing and Jack Grealish has given this side an extra injection of flair and quality.

One of their key strengths has been late goals, equalising in stoppage time against both Bournemouth and Manchester United as well as getting their winner against Wolves in the Carabao Cup with ten minutes left on the clock.

With Tyrique George looking a real threat and Tyler Dibling showing signs of wanting to join the party, there is every chance for Moyes to get the club back into Europe.

Grade: A

Prime Minister's vote: Andy Burnham was cheering on the Toffees during their Carabao Cup victory over Wolves

FULHAM

Position: 19th Points: 2

It has been a truly disastrous start to the campaign for the Cottagers, who remain winless with pressure already being piled on new boss Alvaro Arbeloa.

Fulham took risks in the summer with decision to appoint Arbeloa and back him with several young inexperienced talents from Real Madrid's B team, but it has yet to pay off so far.

After draws in their last two games Fulham will be desperate to finally pick up three points upon return from the international break

The existing squad appear unable or unwilling to adapt to the Spaniard's style of play and are conceding terrible goals at one end and appearing panicked up the other. New boys Shea Charles, Gonzalo Garcia and Cesar Palacios all seem to be talented young players but their inexperience is ultimately hindering their new team.

This is Fulham's worst ever start to a Premier League season and for the first time since their return to the division in 2022 the Cottagers are a relegation worry.

Arbeloa will need to start finding form and fast, the international break will give the players a much-needed rest and give the coach some time which he must use wisely.

Grade: E

Sports.title: Revealed: Jurgen Klopp's list of four rules for Germany's stars in his first managerial job since leaving Liverpool - with WAGs told to stay away, barbers BANNED and new professional standards
Sports.content:
Revealed: Jurgen Klopp's list of four rules for Germany's stars in his first managerial job since leaving Liverpool - with WAGs told to stay away, barbers BANNED and new professional standards

Jurgen Klopp has reportedly introduced four rules for Germany stars as the former Liverpool boss seeks to turn around the fortunes of their national team.

Klopp will take charge of Germany for the first time on Thursday when they face the Netherlands in the Nations League, after being unveiled as the new national team boss back in July.

The 59-year-old, who took the job after a two-year break from the dugout, will hope to restore Germany’s standing after a decade of underperformance at international tournaments.

Klopp succeeded Julian Nagelsmann after Germany crashed out of the World Cup to Paraguay in the last-32, with the presence of players’ WAGs and families placed under the spotlight in the aftermath.

Nagelsmann's partner also made headlines, with German media reporting that his girlfriend, Lena Wurzenberger, was an almost constant presence in the camp.

According to German newspaper Bild, Klopp has sought to significantly restrict their presence as one of four rules for his squad to follow in Germany’s new era.

Jurgen Klopp has introduced four rules for his Germany squad as part of their new era

Players' wives and girlfriends will have limited access during training camps and tournaments

The presence of players' families around the camp was a major talking point during Germany's underwhelming World Cup campaign

The Germany head coach will no longer permit ‘team outings’ during tournaments, which had enabled players’ entire families to visit the team’s headquarters throughout the last World Cup.

Instead, Klopp will reportedly allow families to visit on a limited basis, with the intention that players are able to fully focus on their common goal during training camps and at Euro 2028.

Players have also been banned from being visited by hairdressers at Germany’s team accommodation, with stars instead having to have their hair cut prior to the camp as part of an aim to introduce new professional standards.

Klopp is also reported to have stressed that players must be present for dinner promptly at 7pm or 8pm, rather than arriving gradually, in a move aimed at giving players more time to socialise and connect with each other.

A focus has been placed on encouraging conversations between players in an attempt to grow team unity, including during gym sessions and massages.

As part of the drive, Klopp has banned the use of mobile phones at these times, as well as on matchdays, ensuring his side are focused on essentials in the build-up to their matches.

The rules aimed at improving team culture come with Germany seeking to transform their performances at major tournaments.

Germany have made three consecutive early exits since winning the World Cup in 2014, with group stage eliminations in 2018 and 2022 before a last-32 exit this year.

Klopp has reportedly banned mobile phones at certain times and is encouraging players to socialise more together in an attempt to build team spirit

The national team were also eliminated in the last-16 and quarter-finals of the past two European Championships, with their last semi-final coming back in 2016.

Klopp will assess a 44-man split squad in the first matches of his reign, with the players used across four Nations League fixtures.

The unusually large squad is being separated into two to handle an extended three-week international break, as they face Netherlands, Greece and Serbia.

Klopp has already clashed with German media after his squad selection was leaked earlier this month, while in his first press conference he threatened to resign if his family faces any scrutiny.

After his first game as Germany boss on Thursday, Klopp's side will then take on Greece for the first of two clashes just three days later.

The former Liverpool boss will then switch to his second squad for a clash with Serbia on October 1 before they play Greece again on October 4.

Sports.title: Man Utd news LIVE: JJ Gabriel latest as new deadline set after 'agreement reached'
Sports.content:
Former Man United striker Louis Saha has urged Real Madrid and Barcelona to steer clear of highly-rated youngster JJ Gabriel amid growing interest in the teenager.

He said: "Barcelona and Real Madrid should stay away from JJ Gabriel. I don’t think it is good for the game or the nature of the industry. It seems a terrible message to other young players and their advisors too. Success in football needs patience. You need to work for the opportunity and wait for it to come and then, after you’ve played the games and made that impact, it’s a different conversation.

"Doing really well in the academy, that’s great, but it means nothing in the first team. You don’t get to walk in straight away and replace senior professionals like Matheus Cunha or Bryan Mbeumo or whoever else. That is completely unrealistic and it places too much pressure on a young player. He is the son of a former footballer too. They should know better than to put all this risk on him so early.

"Look at Martin Odegaard. He had all the skills. He looked like he could do it all. He went to Real Madrid and never got his chance. Sometimes you need to protect these players from themselves and their advisors. I can’t understand how they don’t see that for themselves."

He added: "Can JJ Gabriel leave Man United and make an impact at another club as Paul Pogba did at Juventus, or like Jadon Sancho when he left Man City for Borussia Dortmund? I think he is in the sort of position on the pitch where it would be a bit easier to make that breakthrough playing as a forward. In that part of the pitch, you can make mistakes and it is fine. He is not a defender where those mistakes can hurt the team more.

"We saw it with Cristiano Ronaldo at Manchester United when he was young but he was not as young as JJ Gabriel. This is a different situation. There are always exceptions that can be made but the Premier League is a physical competition and JJ Gabriel will get special attention from teams and that will be very hard on him, physically and mentally, no matter what his trajectory could be.

"Paul Pogba and Jadon Sancho were good examples in the past but where are they now in the game? They are no longer in the frame. Not everyone can be Wayne Rooney. He was mature at 16. He had the physique of a monster. JJ Gabriel is not that sort of player, and he will get targeted."

Sports.title: Ex-Liverpool owner George Gillett dies aged 87 after battle with Alzheimer's
Sports.content:
Ex-Liverpool owner George Gillett dies aged 87 after battle with Alzheimer's

American businessman George Gillett, who was previously the co-owner of Liverpool FC, has passed away at the age of 87 following a battle with Alzheimer's Disease

View 2 Images George Gillett (left) with fellow ex-Liverpool co-owner Tom Hicks (Image: Andy Stenning)

Former Liverpool owner George Gillett has died at the age of 87.

‌



The American businessman completed a takeover of Liverpool alongside Tom Hicks in March 2007. They owned the Premier League giants until a bitter sale went through to New England Sports Ventures, a company led by John Henry which would become Fenway Sports Group, in October 2010.

‌



Gillett also used to own ice hockey team Montreal Canadiens, as well as holding stakes in NFL franchise the Miami Dolphins and legendary basketball team Harlem Globetrotters.

‌



“On behalf of the entire Canadiens organization, I would like to extend my deepest condolences to George’s family,” Canadiens owner Geoff Molson said in a statement.

“George immersed himself in the Montreal community and was appreciated by everyone in the organization. We sincerely appreciate his contributions to the Montreal Canadiens during his time as owner.”

‌



Gillett and Hicks took over Liverpool in 2007 following a takeover worth £174million. Their time at the club was a tumultuous one, with fans protesting against their ownership and manager Rafael Benitez clashing with the American pair before their spell in charge came to a bitter end three years later.

After falling out, they were forced to sell to the company that would later become the current owners, Fenway Sports Group, for around £300m - a fee they believed to be well below the club's real value.

View 2 Images Ex-Liverpool owner George Gillett at Anfield in 2009 (Image: AFP/Getty Images)

‌



Gillett made his money through ski resorts. And while he was not popular in Liverpool, his ownership of the Montreal Canadiens from 2001 to 2009 won him many fans in the world of Canadian ice hockey.

National Hockey League (NHL) commissioner Gary Bettman said: “George Gillett’s passion for the Montreal Canadiens and commitment to the city of Montreal were demonstrated throughout his tenure as owner of the storied franchise from 2001 to 2009.

"He guided the Canadiens through a significant chapter in their history that included preparations for their Centennial Celebration, which honoured the franchise’s rich legacy and seminal place in our game.

Article continues below

“George was a friend whose company I always enjoyed, whose counsel was wise, and whose energy was contagious.

"His contributions to the hockey world left an enduring mark, and his legacy will continue to be felt throughout the game for years to come. The National Hockey League sends its heartfelt condolences to his family and many friends.”

Sports.title: Enzo Fernandez transfer statement made as Man City warning issued to Premier League rivals
Sports.content:
Enzo Fernandez transfer statement made as Man City warning issued to Premier League rivals

Enzo Fernandez won the Club World Cup and the UEFA Conference League during his time with Chelsea before moving to Man City during the summer transfer window

View 2 Images Enzo Fernandez has made an instant impact at Manchester City (Image: (Matt McNulty/Getty Images))

Enzo Fernandez has been told he has taken Manchester City from possible Premier League challengers to definite contenders. City spent an eye-watering sum revamping their midfield during the summer, with Fernandez’s British record-equalling £125m move from Chelsea completing their business on deadline day.

The Argentine won the Club World Cup and the UEFA Conference League during his time in London and he has already made an immediate impact at the Etihad. And former City defender Danny Mills, speaking via BestBettingBonuses.co.uk, believes the transfer was a game changer for his old club and has called on people to stop going on about the fee.

“I think the Enzo Fernandez signing was really, really important," he said. "(Ayyoub) Bouaddi is a very, very good player, very talented, but he's very, very young.

“And it's difficult to go through a full season if it was just him and (Elliot) Anderson in there. You'd be thinking, can they survive the whole season? Is there enough creativity in that midfield?

“Suddenly you throw Enzo Fernandez into that, and you've got the likes of (Mateo) Kovacic, incredibly experienced, to drop in and out as well. Suddenly you're going, well, actually, this is now. And this is why I said the Enzo Fernandez signing is a game-changer for City.

“Forget about the fee - the quality and depth that he adds to that midfield takes them from possible challengers to definite challengers.”

City have made an impressive start to the campaign, winning six successive matches in all competitions since a 3-0 defeat to reigning Premier League champions Arsenal in the Community Shield.

And while Mills, who made 53 appearances for City, accepts the Norway international is vital to his old club’s aspirations this season, he does believe they will have a plan in his place if anything happens to him.

“Yes, of course he's vital," he said. "You take him out of the team, you lose 30 goals, 40 goals, 50 goals maybe, whatever it might be.

“So if you did lose him, you've got to try and replace that, which is difficult. But he's fit, he's strong, he's robust. We've seen this time and time again.

“He's scored an obscene amount of goals already this season. So if something did happen, I'm sure there would be a plan, and I'm sure in January they would go again if needed.”

Sports.title: 'Let football fans have a pint — it’s time to scrap this outdated drinking in stands ban'
Sports.content:
The ban on drinking alcohol in the stands is horribly outdated.

And it is great that the United Kingdom has a real football fan as a Prime Minister who is ready to change the law which is so unfair on supporters. Everton fan Andy Burnham is right to speak up and push for supporters to be able to enjoy a pint within sight of the pitch.

You can have a drink at cricket and it is time football fans were allowed to do the same. Times change and it is wrong for football fans to be treated as second class citizens.

In my experience, if you treat people as grown ups - then they will behave like adults. Of course we should be sensitive. Just as we have been in the reintroduction of safe standing. Do it sensibly and, as Burnham suggests, even on a trial basis. Fans will prove him right.

‌



View 2 Images Football's drinking restrictions date back to the hooliganism of the 1980s (Image: PA)

Harry Kane defends Declan Rice after Arsenal star explained England drop out READ MORE :

Harvey Elliott enduring second loan nightmare as Liverpool star branded 'overweight' READ MORE :

No one can forget the booze and drug fuelled scenes outside Wembley ahead of the Euros final in 2021. It has to be policed but being able to drink in your seat would actually ease the binge drinking culture which exists at football games before and at half time.

We have moved on from the bad old days of hooliganism in the 1980s which led to this ban in the first place. Football has a new generation of fans and stadiums are generally safer, there is a different vibe within grounds and it is time to move on.

The other compelling argument which emerged in Tracey Crouch’s independent review into football back in 2021 was that League Two and National League clubs lose up to an estimated £100,000-per-year in sales because of the ban.

‌



This is an important change for all levels of the game - and it is great that we have a PM who understands and respects football fans.

Sports.title: Fellow boss calls for Tonda Eckert to be hit with 'severe' punishment for Spygate plot
Sports.content:
Fellow boss calls for Tonda Eckert to be hit with 'severe' punishment for Spygate plot

Tonda Eckert will discover his punishment from the FA on Thursday having been charged with misconduct for his role in the Southampton Spygate scandal last season

View 2 Images Tonda Eckert is about to discover his fate (Image: Matt Watson/Southampton FC via Getty Images)

Southampton manager Tonda Eckert deserves a "severe" punishment from the FA for the Spygate scandal, according to Cambridge United boss Neil Harris.

‌



Eckert will discover his fate on Thursday at an FA hearing, having admitted giving the order for a junior member of staff to spy on three rival clubs' training sessions. Southampton were chucked out of the Championship play-off final in May and docked four points this season by the EFL.

‌



But now Saints are braced for further punishment, with the FA set to announce its decision on Eckert, having charged him with misconduct back in July. The 33-year-old has pleaded for forgiveness in a four-hour meeting with the FA, but could be given a hefty ban.

‌



"[I'm talking] on behalf of myself but probably also every other manager in the Football League and a lot of fans as well," Harris told BBC Radio 5 Live.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"What happened is bordering on disgraceful. Listening to their CEO (Phil Parsons) saying they've been punished enough, the football club; I agree - Southampton Football Club and the fanbase and the workforce have been punished hugely.

"Tonda has owned it and said it was his decision to spy and send a junior member of staff. He's owned it and the club have decided to stick with him.

"The manager should get a huge ban, in my opinion, as a senior football man in this country. He's gone way across the mark of cheating. We don't do that in this country. There's no place for it in the game over here and it deserves a ban.

‌



View 2 Images Tonda Eckert was behind Southampton spying on rival club's training sessions (Image: Matt Watson/Getty Images)

"I've seen a couple of bits recently saying it should be two or four-game ban. We're talking about basically cheating and trying to gain an advantage on the opponent.

"So, as you can tell, I feel quite strongly about it - and it's not just me, it's every manager in the Football League that agrees. I think whatever punishment he gets needs to be severe and it needs to be stamped down on. It can't happen again."

‌



Saints chief executive Parsons told the BBC that he felt the club had "taken enough" from the EFL's punishment for what it called a "contrived and determined plan" to spy on Oxford United, Ipswich and Middlesbrough. That is the belief of ex-Southampton striker Charlie Austin.

“I think we should just move on," he told The Sun. “The punishment has been done. They got taken out of this game, which is worth millions.

“Eckert is a young coach. He made a mistake, he’s admitted he’s made a mistake, and he’s learned from it. Just let him get on with his career now. It’s ridiculous this has been dragged out further.”

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo vows to carry on playing for Portugal and targets 1,000-goal landmark
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo vows to carry on playing for Portugal and targets 1,000-goal landmark

Cristiano Ronaldo has decided to keep playing for Portugal at the age of 41, despite suffering huge disappointment at the World Cup and facing increased criticism over his performances

View 2 Images Cristiano Ronaldo is still going at the age of 41 (Image: Fadel SENNA / AFP via Getty Images)

Cristiano Ronaldo has hit back at his critics and vowed to carry on playing for Portugal as he nears 1,000 career goals.

‌



Ronaldo's future in international football was in doubt following the World Cup, but the 41-year-old is playing on after Jorge Jesus replaced Roberto Martinez as manager. Ronaldo has 146 goals in 233 appearances for his country and is approaching a personal landmark.

‌



The Al-Nassr striker sits on 979 career goals for club and country ahead of Portugal beginning their Nations League campaign against Wales in Lisbon on Thursday night. While he has denied that his decision to continue playing for Portugal was driven by his own goal tally, Ronaldo did admit he'd like to reach four figures while on international duty.

‌



Portugal were dumped out of the World Cup by bitter rivals Spain in the last 16 and the 1-0 defeat did give Ronaldo pause for thought. Asked if he considered retiring, he replied: “Yes I did.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"Of course, I’m always thinking on my decisions, my future, the present also. I’m a thinker. You have to think. This is why you see me here now. It means I will continue.

“I had a conversation with our president, with our coach. I still believe that I’m able to help the national team to reach what they want, and will finish when I feel like I’m not doing anything here.

“I think I can give to the national team my support, not only through the goals, but also outside of football. This is a new young generation. But for me the basic point is to be able on the pitch to score the goals and to help the team win games.”

‌



View 2 Images Jorge Jesus has taken over as Portugal boss (Image: Patricia de Melo Moreira / AFP via Getty Images)

The veteran forward now wants to help bring through the next generation. “I know why young kids love Cristiano, because they see me as an example, and I will continue to do that. Even when I am retired… in 10 years," he joked.

“I’m happy with myself. It doesn’t matter if I play tomorrow, if I rest the next game, for me the most important thing is that I feel good.”

‌



Ronaldo's place in the starting XI has become a hot topic of debate in Portugal. He insists that it doesn't bother him. "I said it quite often at home with my friends. I’ve been playing football for so many years, I have been welcome almost everywhere, apart from a few exceptions," Ronaldo said.

“I feel the Portuguese fans like me, but I do understand that some TV channels want to criticise me – they’ve tried to kill me, but only with a shotgun.

“They are dying for me not to come to the national team anymore, but I can still move away from it. Anyway, I am used to it. For over 20 years I have been doing this, but my memories are with people who love me.”

Sports.title: 'I'm not fine with Ronnie O'Sullivan - I don't want anything to do with him'
Sports.content:
'I'm not fine with Ronnie O'Sullivan - I don't want anything to do with him'

Ali Carter and Ronnie O'Sullivan have had a strained relationship, despite being friends as teenagers

View 2 Images Ronnie O'Sullivan has had a strained relationship with some of his rivals over the years (Image: Tai Chengzhe/VCG via Getty Images)

Ali Carter has admitted that he wants nothing to do with Ronnie O’Sullivan, despite the two being friends early in their careers. The duo used to train together at Witham Snooker Bowl.

‌



Carter credits O'Sullivan for helping him to win a championship, but then claims that their friendship went downhill. The two have come up against each other 29 times in their careers, with O’Sullivan winning 25, but some of those matches haven’t been without incident.

‌



Speaking on the Talking Snooker podcast, Carter said: “Me and Ronnie, we used to practise together, as a 17-year-old at Witham Snooker Bowl. We played every single day.

‌



Ali Carter reveals phone call with Ronnie O'Sullivan's dad during cancer treatment READ MORE :

“That was what led up to winning the Benson & Hedges Championship in 1999. That was a big tournament then and if it wasn’t for him getting me prepped up, I probably would never have won that tournament.”

However, despite that early friendship, Carter outlined how things changed. “So, after spending a lot of time with Ronnie, and he probably knew at the time how good I was, I just felt that when we went to tournaments, he wasn’t really the same toward me,” he said.

“Looking back, I probably took it personally. I think he’s like that with everyone, it wasn’t just me. But I’m not everyone, am I?

‌



“I can only speak from my own perspective. So, I just thought, well, if he can’t be bothered to talk to me, then I can’t be bothered to talk to him. That’s fine. We both know where we stand then.”

View 2 Images Ali Carter has spoken about his relationship with Ronnie O'Sullivan. (Image: Tai Chengzhe/VCG via Getty Images)

There was, however, an incident during the 2018 World Championships in Sheffield in which the two appeared to shoulder-barge during their match. Carter remembers an apology from O’Sullivan over the incident, but then recalled how their relationship soured again.

‌



He said: “We were at the Novotel in York, and he was with Damien Hirst and all his cronies, and I was having breakfast. Ronnie came over to me, he said, ‘Listen, I’m really sorry about what happened in Sheffield’.

“Then lockdown happened and all the tournaments were in Milton Keynes, so I played Ronnie O’Sullivan in the semi-finals of the [2020] Northern Ireland Open at Milton Keynes.

“I’d done an interview with Alan McManus before and he said, ‘It’s always a needle match between you and Ronnie.’ I said, ‘No, not at all. He came up to me in the Novotel in York and he apologised and I apologised. It’s all water under the bridge.’

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

“So, anyway, he beat me, then the next tournament, I’ve come out of the tournament office. He must have seen my interview and he’s gone, ‘I never apologised to you. That was your fault.’

“I said, ‘What? So I just made it up then, did I? That you come up to me in York and apologised?’ He went, ‘Yeah, you did,’ and then had a little laugh, and that was that.

Article continues below

“You can’t comprehend what’s just happened. Is he getting me at it or what? And I just thought, right, okay, he wants to say that, whatever. The only way I can take myself out of that situation is just have nothing to do with it anymore, not speak to him. It’s pointless.”

Reflecting on their current relationship, Carter added: “I mean, me and Ronnie…we’re not fine, [but] there’s nothing. There’s no relationship there, there’s no hate, there’s no nothing.”

The most recent meeting between the two was in January this year, in the last 32 of the German Masters. That match saw Carter come out as 5-3 winner.

Sports.title: Harry Kane defends Declan Rice after Arsenal star explained England drop out
Sports.content:
Harry Kane defends Declan Rice after Arsenal star explained England drop out

Declan Rice was one of five players to pull out of the England squad for the four Nations League games in the current international break, but Harry Kane understands his reasoning

View 2 Images Harry Kane received a message from Declan Rice (Image: Julian Finney/FIFA via Getty Images)

Declan Rice “reached out” to Harry Kane to explain why he pulled out of England duty.

‌



Arsenal midfielder Rice was one of five players, along with Cole Palmer, Marcus Rashford, Robbie Mainoo and Tino Livramento, to withdraw from the squad for the Nations League fixtures, with Morgan Gibbs-White and James Garner called up as replacements.

‌



Kane was highly critical of nine players pulling out in November 2024 by insisting “England comes before everything” but was more sympathetic this time.

‌



Palmer missed the World Cup and had played the whole 90 minutes of Chelsea ’s last four Premier League games, but Rice struggled in the World Cup because he played 69 games for club and country last season.

England captain Kane said: “Look, everyone has their own situation. I know how tough the summer was and I know especially in the Premier League how gruelling that schedule is. I'm in a different situation now where I have the winter break and I have moments to recharge and refresh. Some of the players don't get that.

‌



“Everyone has to look after themselves and put themselves first, and I trust all the boys. I spoke to Dec, and I know Dec goes far and beyond for the club and country, so I know how much he gives and I know he's been struggling for a while with his issues.

“Some someone like Dec has to get himself sorted and get himself fresh, and he has big games for club, big games for country coming up. You know, there's situations where you've got to do what you've got to do, and that's between the coach and the player.

View 2 Images Harry Kane has been training with his England teammates at St George's Park (Image: Harriet Massey/Getty Images)

‌



“I've not spoken to Cole, no. Dec just reached out to me just personally. He just sent me a message, just kind of voice noted me. They don't have to talk to me. I know they spoke to the coach, so, yeah, that's down to the players.”

England host Spain at Wembley on Saturday before heading to Prague to play Czechia next Tuesday. Tuchel's side then head to Rijeka to play Croatia on October 3 before finally hosting Czechia at Wembley on October 6.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
