World.title: Chipangali drug stock stable
World.content:
The Department of Health Services in Chipangali District in Eastern Province has said that clinical services in the district are currently stable with drug availability above 89 percent.

Speaking during a senior management meeting held at the District Administration Office, District Clinical Care Officer Geoffrey Ndhlovu said the 89 percent drug availability in the district reflects adequate essential medicines, essential supplies and vaccines.

Mr Ndhlovu added that three more health facilities have been opened in the district bringing the total number of health facilities to 27.

“We have opened three more health facilities in the district namely Nguluwe, Nyauzi, and Kapatamoyo health facilities which are already providing outpatient health services,” Mr Ndhlovu said.

He however mentioned that the new facilities are not fully operational as they still face challenges relating to inadequate essential equipment and supplies.

“Currently we are not conducting deliveries in these new facilities, because the equipment we have can only support outpatient care,” he said.

He said the department has since requested for equipment through the Constituency Development Fund (CDF), noting that the request was approved and awaits funding.

Meanwhile Mr Ndhlovu disclosed that the department has conducted 297 cesarean section surgeries from October 2025 to date.

He said the surgeries were conducted within the district at Muzeyi Clinic.

Mr Ndhlovu reported that all the surgeries were successful without any complications.

“All women who may require advanced care are referred to Muzeyi, so that they wait to deliver safely. So, the facility sometimes has inadequate space. In view of this, we are also lobbying for construction of a mother’s shelter and ablution block so that our mothers are well kept as they wait to be operated on,” Mr Ndhlovu said.

World.title: Zambia, European Union reaffirm longstanding partnership
World.content:
Zambia and the European Union (EU) have reaffirmed their longstanding partnership, underscoring shared commitments to democracy, rule of law, and economic cooperation.

European Commissioner for International Partnerships, Jozef Síkela, has commended Zambia’s standing as a beacon of democracy and encouraged both sides to maintain respect for the rule of law while advancing a forward-looking partnership.

This is according to a statement issued to the media in Lusaka by First Secretary for Press and Public Relations at Zambia’s Permanent Mission to the United Nations, Namatama Njekwa.

Ms Njekwa revealed that the remarks were made during a bilateral meeting on the sidelines of the 81st United Nations General Assembly (UNGA81).

She noted that the EU reaffirmed its support for Zambia’s leadership in promoting multilateralism and the rules-based international order, while both parties agreed to deepen cooperation through investment, value addition, and initiatives aligned with the Grow Zambia Agenda.

She added that Mr Síkela highlighted Africa’s critical role in electric-vehicle battery and mineral value chains, with Zambia welcoming the EU’s Global Gateway initiative and development cooperation, including budget support of approximately EUR 110 million.

Ms Njekwa further stated that both sides emphasised that post-election developments should not detract from opportunities to strengthen economic ties.

She indicated that the meeting also reaffirmed collaboration on international peace and security, with both Zambia and the EU pledging to prioritise the consolidation of their partnership.

World.title: Nalolo’s Kaunga Lueti in water blues
World.content:
Nalolo District Commissioner Namatama Mupo has called for an urgent solution to the water crisis that has hit Kaunga Lueti community in Nalolo West Bank.

The media reports that the water reticulation plant at Kaunga Lueti Primary School, which services about 4,000 people, has been non-operational since the first week of September, 2026.

An assessment conducted by Nalolo Town Council after the community reported the matter, established that the pump controller and surge protective device need replacement.

Speaking during an urgent District Disaster Management Committee (DDMC) meeting held at her office, Mrs Mupo said water issues are critical and require urgent attention as they affect the community and public institutions such as Kaunga Lueti Primary School, the health post and the police post.

“Water is life and as such, there is a need to tackle water issues with urgency, as delaying would lead to waterborne diseases and possible closure of the school where the water scheme is located,” said Mrs Mupo.

She has since directed the DDMC to write to the local authority to request for funds under the Constituency Development Fund (CDF) Disaster Management and Mitigation Unit (DMMU) component so that the water plant can be repaired.

And District Disaster Management Officer Annie Phiri assured the District Commissioner that documents requesting for funds will be prepared and once the funds are available, the committee will ensure that the water plant is worked so that the Kaunga Lueti community can have access to clean and safe water again.

Ms Phiri said the water plant is important as it is the only source of clean and safe water in the area, hence the need to find a solution as soon as possible.

Meanwhile, District Education Board Secretary (DEBS) Muyoba Liwakala said there is a need to set up a committee that will be in charge of the water scheme to ensure regular maintenance and avoid future breakdowns.

Mr Liwakala said the water reticulation facility is a huge investment that needs to be maintained at all times so that it can stand the test of time.

The District Commissioner also called on the Department of Agriculture to intensify El Nino sensitisation meetings so that farmers are well prepared and take preventive measures before disasters strike.

Mrs Mupo said following the rains experienced in some parts of the province, some farmers are confused on whether to start farming or wait for the usual planting period.

Responding to the DC, Acting Nalolo District Agricultural Coordinator (DACO) Patience Munalula said El Nino sensitisation meetings are ongoing and Agriculture Camp Officers are currently engaging farmers on venturing into smart agriculture and what to expect in view of climate change effects.

World.title: Silondwa wins Discover golf title
World.content:
Nkana golfer Kedrick Silondwa survived a three-way countback to win the Discover Insurance Golf Championship at Nkana Golf Club.

Silondwa, off handicap 12, carded 42 points to top a tightly contested field and walk away with a K3,500 voucher and the overall winner’s trophy.

“It’s been a great day of golf and I can only thank Discover Insurance for deciding to spend their fourth birthday with us. We hope to see more of you around. To the players, I wish to thank you as well. It was really competitive and you made me work hard for my reward,” he said after receiving the trophy.

In the men’s category, Sam Mpundu also finished with 42 points to claim top prize on countback ahead of Tashbekov Djurabek, with Frank Masaka third on 35 points.

In the women’s category, Gladys Mudenda won outright with 35 points, one better than Emma Makoni, while Elisa Manjolo was third on 33 points.

In the subsidiary prizes, Mpundu won the nearest-to-the-pin award, Wiaan Le Roux won the longest drive in the men’s section, while Manjolo took the women’s award.

Discover Insurance Vice-Board Chairperson Chisuwo Hamwela said the tournament was organised to commemorate the company’s fourth anniversary and support the Grow Zambia Agenda.

“We are happy to celebrate our fourth anniversary with the business community and it’s been great. But on top of that, we are game for the Grow Zambia Agenda and while it is important to grow the economy, it is equally important to expand growth to other areas,” Hamwela said.

“Nkana Golf Club is doing that with its efforts with the junior golf programme and we are more than happy to supplement that with donations to the junior programme. At this tournament, we held a junior event and donated prizes in the form of school bags and more than a hundred golf balls.”

In the junior chipping contest, Peter Kasongo, Blessing Mambwe and Grace Washeni emerged winners.

World.title: Africa: All of Africa Today - September 23, 2026
World.content:
UN Chief Says Security Council Remains 'Unjust' Without Permanent African Seat

UN Secretary-General António Guterres has said the lack of a permanent seat for Africa on the UN Security Council is no longer defensible. Guterres made the remarks on Tuesday, September 22, while addressing the opening of the 81st session of the UN General Assembly in New York - his final General Assembly opening address before his term ends on December 31, 2026.

"The Security Council was designed in the aftermath of World War II. But the world has fundamentally changed since then," Guterres told world leaders. He pointed specifically to Africa, saying that most of the continent was under colonial rule when the United Nations was established in 1945. His remarks come amid renewed global momentum around UN reform.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

Eleven Killed in Mass Shooting in South Africa's KZN Province

Eleven people were killed and three others wounded after gunmen opened fire inside a residence in KwaMakhutha, south of Durban, on Tuesday night. Police reported that 13 men and a pregnant woman were attending a gathering in the Ziko area when three men arrived and opened fire. Ten victims, including the woman, died at the scene, while another succumbed to injuries in the hospital.

A police spokesperson confirmed that a manhunt is underway. Preliminary investigations indicate that several victims were previously known to Crime Intelligence regarding alleged illegal activities, though further details are being withheld to protect the ongoing investigation.

Niger's Junta Strips Five More Exiled Critics of Nationality

Niger's military junta has stripped five more exiled opposition figures of their citizenship, extending a controversial policy targeting critics of the administration, according to Human Rights Watch (HRW).

On September 17, 2026, junta leader Abdourahamane Tiani signed a decree revoking the nationality of the prominent Nigeriens living abroad. The decree stems from a 2024 executive order establishing a national terrorism database - a tool HRW criticizes for overbroad inclusion criteria, inadequate due process, and heightened risks of statelessness.

"The Niger junta has been depriving perceived political opponents of their nationality without meaningful due process, and contrary to Niger's obligations to prevent statelessness and protect fundamental rights," said Ilaria Allegrozzi, HRW's senior Sahel researcher.

Moroccans Head to Polls as Youth Unemployment Takes Center Stage

More than 15 million registered voters are set to elect members of Morocco's lower house of parliament. Wednesday's vote marks the first general election since a Gen Z-led protest movement brought thousands of young people into the streets last year to demand employment, improved healthcare and education, and relief from the rising cost of living.

Frustrations resurfaced in July when large numbers of young Moroccans attempted to cross into the Spanish enclave of Ceuta in search of work in Europe. Consequently, job creation and youth engagement have become central campaign promises across the political spectrum. However, while some young voters see the ballot box as a vehicle for reform, others express little confidence that the outcome will improve their daily lives.

Close 

U.S. to End Health Funding in Zimbabwe After Rejected Deal

The U.S. government will conclude its health assistance programs in Zimbabwe at the end of September following Harare's decision to decline a new bilateral funding model over data privacy concerns. Over the last two decades, the U.S. has played a key role in supporting Zimbabwean public health, including funding antiretroviral drugs (ARVs) for HIV treatment and stipends for healthcare workers.

"Because of that, Zimbabwe has achieved HIV epidemic control, with more than 95% of people living with HIV receiving treatment," said U.S. Ambassador Pamela Tremont, emphasizing that sustaining those gains must remain the primary goal under local leadership.

Ambassador Tremont said the U.S. has updated its global health delivery model around a new Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) framework requiring co-investment from host nations. Following Zimbabwe's rejection of the bilateral agreement, U.S.-funded health operations are set to wrap up on September 30.

World.title: Congo-Kinshasa: DR Congo Ebola Outbreak Toll Exceeds 3,700 Deaths
World.content:
More than 130 days into the latest Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), health experts said on Wednesday that response efforts have been scaled up significantly and "the first encouraging signs of progress" are now being seen.

In an update, the UN World Health Organization (WHO) said that in the last 21 days, cases of infection fell by approximately 26 per cent in province of Ituri and by 15 per cent in the province of Haut Uele.

However, over the same period, North Kivu province recorded a 73 per cent increase, clearly indicating that the Ebola Bundibugyo outbreak has a different transmission profile in the seven affected provinces where it has been confirmed.

"While cases and theft are declining in some provinces, they continue to rise in others," said WHO Regional Emergency Director for Africa, Dr Marie Roseline Belizaire.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

"Those patterns show the outbreak is still not under control and remain spread across a wide geographic area. One of our greatest concerns is that too many people are still dying before reaching treatment."

Dr Belizaire explained that around one in three new cases of infection are only identified after people have died outside Ebola treatment centres, in the community.

"These are lives that could potentially have been saved through earlier detection and timely access to care," the WHO medic said, adding that every death in the community increases the risk of further transmission among family members, caregivers and others involved in traditional burial practices.

Children at most risk

Although adults account for most confirmed cases of infection, children under five have the highest case fatality rate, at more than 60 per cent, compared with approximately 40 per cent among adults.

Ebola infections in children under 5 are proving very hard to detect because they "can't necessarily explain their signs and symptoms as well as adults, and the presentation (of symptoms) may be confusing," added WHO medic Dr. Catherine Smallwood.

Youngsters also account for a disproportionate share of those dying in the community and in health facilities where Ebola is not diagnosed in time.

"We must do more to identify sick children earlier and ensure that they receive appropriate treatment without delay; early detection save lives," Dr Belizaire stressed, in an online update from Kinshasa.

Ongoing efforts to ramp up the disease outbreak response have contributed to higher success in tracing contacts of infected people, now at almost 88 per cent.

But "too many new infections are still being detected without a known epidemiological link; closing the surveillance gap is essential, and we are to detect cases earlier, trace their contact, and interrupt every chain of transmission," Dr. Belizaire insisted.

Expanding response

The UN agency and partners continue to expand their reach across affected provinces, with nearly 1,400 treatment and isolation beds across 49 Ebola treatment centres. In addition, there are 25 laboratories capable of processing up to 2,500 tests every day.

However, infrastructure alone will not stop the outbreak, she said.

"Our response is no longer simply about the scaling up everywhere; it is about directing teams, expertise, and resources to the areas where transmission is greatest and where the risks are high."

Speaking from Beni in North Kivu, WHO's Dr Smallwood highlighted the "massive mobilization" of responders in recent weeks, in response to the worrying spread of infection in rural areas of DR Congo.

However, although new health centre or Ebola treatment centre beds are becoming available every day, "the big challenge now is finding the partners that can work within those health facilities...The human resources gap is one of the biggest gaps," Dr. Smallwood explained.

The WHO medic underscored the need to shift the response "from the big urban centres of Beni, Butembo and Katwa in North Kivu to the province's remote villages.

"Distances are really long and it takes a long time for patients to be referred into the urban centres," she said. "So, we really need to put priority on decentralising the response to where the cases are into the villages and into the local areas."

Ebola facts

Close 

Ebola disease is a severe, often fatal illness affecting humans and other primates.

The virus is transmitted to people from wild animals (such as fruit bats, porcupines and non-human primates); it then spreads in the human population through direct contact with the blood, secretions, organs or other bodily fluids of infected people. It can also be transmitted by contact with bedding or clothing contaminated with these fluids.

The average Ebola disease case fatality rate is around 50 per cent, according to WHO. Case fatality rates have varied from 25 to 90 per cent in past outbreaks.

The first Ebola disease outbreaks occurred in remote villages in Central Africa, near tropical rainforests.

The 2014-2016 Ebola virus disease outbreak in West Africa was the largest and most complex Ebola outbreak since the virus was first discovered in 1976.

There were more cases and deaths in this outbreak than all others combined. It also spread between countries, starting in Guinea then moving across land borders to Sierra Leone and Liberia.

World.title: Malawi: Malawi Puts $1,000 Limit On Cash in Your Pocket
World.content:
Malawians and visitors alike are facing a dramatic new crackdown on cash, after the Reserve Bank of Malawi (RBM) slapped sweeping restrictions on the physical possession and movement of foreign currency -- with anyone caught holding more than $1,000 without central bank permission now at risk.

Under the astonishing new rules, anyone physically carrying more than US$1,000 -- roughly K1.75 million -- or its equivalent in another foreign currency, must first secure the blessing of the central bank, or risk falling foul of the law.

The eyebrow-raising restrictions are laid out in the Foreign Exchange (Limit on Physical Possession of Foreign Currency) Notice, 2026, quietly issued by the central bank on September 7 and published in the Malawi Government Gazette on September 18.



Anyone attempting to take or send more than $1,000 out of the country will now be forced to prove the cash was purchased from an authorised dealer -- or otherwise obtain explicit permission from the RBM before crossing the border.

It doesn't stop there. The central bank has also clamped down on how much Malawi kwacha can leave the country without its say-so.

Cross-border traders will be permitted to carry kwacha equivalent to up to $5,000, but ordinary travellers face a far stingier cap -- just $100.

The dramatic tightening of the rules comes as Malawi grapples with a punishing foreign exchange shortage and a booming black market in forex, with authorities apparently determined to choke off unofficial cash flows once and for all.

Travellers, businesses and everyday citizens dealing in foreign currency now find themselves under far greater scrutiny, particularly when large sums of cash are involved.

The RBM has left no room for ambiguity, making clear that any foreign currency exceeding the new threshold simply cannot be carried across Malawi's borders without the correct paperwork or central bank sign-off.

The crackdown lands against the backdrop of Malawi's long-running forex crisis, which has left the country starved of hard currency, disrupted access to vital imports, and piled pressure on the wider economy.

In effect, the central bank has handed itself sweeping new powers to monitor exactly how much physical foreign currency is leaving Malawi -- and to demand answers over where that money came from.

For everyday travellers, it's the eye-catching $1,000 possession threshold that will raise the most eyebrows, while cross-border traders must now operate within a separate $5,000 kwacha limit.

The bombshell new rules mark a major escalation in Malawi's battle to rein in foreign currency flows, as authorities scramble to contain a forex crisis that shows little sign of easing.

World.title: Africa: Political Communication in Africa - More Than Elections
World.content:
Winnie Gor, founder of Communications Africa and member of the Female Founders Initiative Global 50 Under 50 Class of 2026.

Nairobi — As countries across Africa gear up for national elections, political communications is a strategic function of governance.

We often picture political communication as campaign billboards, posters, cheering crowds at rallies, and speeches on television and radio.

In Africa, political communication tends to be most visible during election campaigns, but its role does not begin or end at the ballot box. It shapes how political leaders build trust, communicate policies, respond to crises, influence public opinion and – ultimately - maintain relationships with citizens.



Political communication is not new to Africa, nor is it simply an import of Western democratic practice. Throughout African history, communities have relied on chieftaincies, councils of elders, monarchies, community structures and storytelling as important spaces for dialogue, collective decision-making and the exchange of information. What has changed in the contemporary era is not the existence of political communication, but its reach, speed and complexity.

Direct access to voters brings new opportunities but also new risks.

Today, a political message can move from a local community meeting to WhatsApp, TikTok, television, radio and international media within minutes. Political leaders can communicate directly with millions of citizens without relying entirely on conventional media gatekeepers. But this unprecedented reach also comes with new risks. Messages can be misinterpreted, taken out of context or amplified before there is an opportunity to clarify them. Misinformation, disinformation, malinformation and online outrage can shape public opinion alongside accurate and verified information.

This is where strategic political communication becomes critical.

Communication in politics should not simply be about whether a politician is a good speaker or can deliver a compelling speech. It should involve understanding audiences, anticipating how messages will be received, selecting the right channels, communicating clearly and, most importantly, listening to citizens. It requires deliberate planning, implementation and evaluation rather than the ad hoc communication that often emerges only when a political challenge or crisis has already occurred.

It is particularly important in Africa, where political communication takes place across diverse socio-cultural, linguistic and media environments. A message that resonates with a young, digitally connected audience in an urban centre may not have the same meaning or relevance in a rural community. An official government statement may be factually accurate, yet still fail to connect with citizens if it does not explain what a policy means for their everyday lives.

The problem, therefore, is not whether African political leaders are communicating. They are communicating constantly. The question is whether they are communicating strategically, responsibly and with a genuine understanding of their audiences.

This distinction matters because political communication shapes more than election outcomes. It influences how citizens understand government policies, engage with public institutions, respond to crises, and develop or lose confidence in those institutions. Effective political communication must therefore extend beyond electoral campaigns to encompass governance, policy messaging, internal cohesion, public opinion, and crisis management. These interconnected dimensions, how governments explain policies, how leaders communicate during crises, and how institutions coordinate internally, directly influence public trust and the coherence of the message presented externally.

Politicians often treat communication as an afterthought, rather than a chance to create trust and engagement.

The problem is that communication is too often treated as an afterthought: something to deploy when there is a crisis, an election, a public backlash or a damaging news cycle. But by the time a crisis emerges, it may already be too late to build the trust that effective crisis communication requires.

This presents both a challenge and an opportunity for Africa. Political communication needs to be understood not as political spin, but as a professional and strategic function of politics and governance.

The rise of digital media has made this even more urgent. Africa has a young and increasingly digitally connected population, while citizens are also demanding greater transparency, responsiveness and accountability from political leaders and institutions. Political actors can no longer assume that communication is a one-way process in which leaders speak and citizens simply listen. Citizens now respond, question, challenge, fact-check, remix and redistribute political messages in real time.

As the environment changes, political leaders and institutions need to invest not only in communication platforms, but also in communication capacity. It requires professionals who understand audiences, data, media ecosystems, digital behaviour and the political and cultural contexts in which messages are received. It also requires greater professionalism and ethical standards within the field.

Close 

Effective communication builds meaningful relationships between political institutions and the people they serve.

Most importantly, Africa should not simply replicate political communication models developed elsewhere. The continent has its own communication traditions, political realities and rapidly evolving media ecosystems. Strategic political communication should therefore be rooted in African contexts while responding to the realities of an increasingly interconnected world.

Political communication is ultimately about more than crafting the right message. It is about building meaningful relationships between political institutions and the people they serve. Africa does not simply need more political messages. It needs better, more strategic and more responsible political communication before, during and long after the elections.

Winnie Gor is a strategic communications expert, entrepreneur, and founder of Communications Africa and was selected for the Female Founders Initiative Global 50 Under 50 Class of 2026.

World.title: Ghana: Bishops Raise the Alarm - Ghana Is Becoming a Cocaine Hub
World.content:
Accra — "The seizure in France of a large shipment of cocaine from Ghana must not be treated as an isolated incident, but as part of a wider problem," the Bishops of Ghana said following the seizure by French customs authorities on 10 September of 3.9 tonnes of cocaine, with an estimated value of €225 million (approximately US$261.45 million). The drugs were hidden inside a container carrying plastic waste, which had arrived at the northern French port of Dunkirk from Ghana.

"This seizure is one episode within a wider problem. Ghana's geographical position and participation in international trade make vigilance at our ports, airports and borders especially important," said the statement signed by Matthew Kwasi Gyamfi, Bishop of Sunyani and President of the Ghana Catholic Bishops' Conference (GCBC).

Ghana is not only a transit country used by drug traffickers, but has also become a country where drugs are consumed. "We are equally troubled by the domestic face of this menace: drug abuse among young people, the corrosive effect of drug money on our institutions, and the temptation it poses to persons in positions of trust, whether in commerce, the security services or, we say with sorrow, within the Church herself," the Bishops said.

After appealing to the authorities to step up the fight against drug trafficking and help people struggling with drug addiction to escape their "ordeal", the GCBC stressed that "this battle cannot be left to the Government alone".

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

"We call upon Catholic parishes, schools and youth organisations to intensify drug-prevention education, mentorship and pastoral accompaniment, and urge priests, consecrated persons, catechists and lay leaders to address the issue courageously in their preaching and catechesis," the statement continued.

Addressing young people directly, the Bishops concluded with an appeal: "Do not be deceived by the temporary gains promised by the drug trade. Choose life. Build your future upon honest work, faith, education, virtue and service. Your dignity is beyond price, and the Church stands ready to accompany you."

World.title: South Sudan: South Sudan's Kiir Dissolves Transitional Government
World.content:
South Sudan's President Salva Kiir dissolved the transitional unity government and appointed a caretaker administration ahead of country's first general elections due in December.

The changes, announced in a presidential order read on state-owned South Sudan Broadcasting Corporation on Tuesday, September 22, removed the vice presidents, ministers and local administrators and dissolved the national and state legislative assemblies.

ALSO READ: South Sudan: AU urges permanent ceasefire, full implementation of peace accord

Kiir remains president during the electoral period until a newly elected president is sworn in, according to the order.

The caretaker administration includes 13 national ministries, 10 state governors and chief administrators for Abyei, Greater Pibor and Ruweng administrative areas.

The dissolution follows amendments to the National Elections Act signed into law by Kiir on Monday. The amendments removed previous legal requirements linking the elections to completion of a permanent constitution and a national population and housing census.

Kiir has led South Sudan since the country's independence from Sudan in 2011.

The National Elections Commission is preparing to begin voter registration ahead of the December 22 polls.

The caretaker arrangement replaces the power-sharing government established under a 2018 peace agreement.

World.title: Mozambique: U.S. to Disburse 1.5 Million Dollars for Weapons Control
World.content:
Maputo — The United States government has pledged to disburse 1.5 million dollars to strengthen Mozambique's management of weapons and ammunition, as part of a program aimed at strengthening security in the country.

The initiative, funded by the US Government in collaboration with The HALO Trust USA, is designed to prevent conventional arms intended for public protection from being used by criminals and terrorist groups. It focuses on enhancing the capacity of security personnel through specialized training in management, control, and security of arms and ammunition.

The program comes at a time when proper control of arsenals and weapons stockpiles is considered crucial to reducing the risks of illegal diversion of arms and ammunition. The US Department of State itself frames this type of cooperation within its strategy to prevent the illegal proliferation of small arms and light weapons and to strengthen stockpile security.

Capacity building for Mozambican professionals constitutes a central component of the initiative. The objective is to equip security forces with the knowledge and tools needed to improve arsenal management, strengthen control mechanisms, and reduce the possibility of arms and ammunition being diverted into criminal activities.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

Cooperation between the two countries in this field is not new. According to the US Department of State, the United States resumed cooperation with Mozambique in conventional weapons destruction in 2022, supporting projects aimed at strengthening the capacity of security forces to manage arms and ammunition and prevent their illicit diversion.

In 2023, US assistance included the construction and installation of mobile armories, as well as stockpile management and security training for Mozambican security forces.

Effective arms and ammunition control seeks to minimize the likelihood of state weaponry falling into the hands of criminal networks or groups involved in acts of violence and terrorism.

For Mozambique, the initiative also represents a strengthening of international cooperation in the security sector and in the capacity building of national institutions.

The partnership between Mozambique, the United States, and The HALO Trust USA thus aims to contribute to a safer and more responsible weapons management system, reducing the risks associated with improper storage, weapons diversion, and the illegal circulation of ammunition.

This cooperation is part of a broader trajectory of US support for Mozambique in conventional weapons destruction.

Department of State data point out that, between 1993 and 2023, the United States allocated approximately 57.9 million dollars to various initiatives related to conventional weapons destruction, humanitarian mine action, and capacity building in the country.

World.title: Africa: Guterres - UN Security Council Remains 'Unjust' Without Permanent African Seat
World.content:
UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres has renewed calls for reform of the United Nations Security Council, saying Africa's continued lack of a permanent seat is no longer defensible.

Guterres made the remarks on Tuesday, September 22, while addressing the opening of the 81st session of the UN General Assembly in New York, in what was his final General Assembly opening address as secretary-general. His term ends on December 31, 2026.

"The Security Council was designed in the aftermath of World War II. But the world has fundamentally changed since then," Guterres told world leaders.

He pointed specifically to Africa, noting that most of the continent was still under colonial rule when the United Nations was created in 1945.



ALSO READ: What to know ahead of UN General Assembly

"Today, Africa still has no permanent representation on the Council," he said. "A 21st century Security Council without permanent African seats is unjust and indefensible. This must change."

Guterres's remarks come amid renewed international discussions over reforming the Security Council, whose permanent membership remains limited to China, France, Russia, the United Kingdom and the United States.

The African Union has long called for greater representation on the UN most powerful organ, including permanent seats for African countries under the Common African Position outlined in the Ezulwini Consensus and Sirte Declaration.

ALSO READ: Michelle Bachelet withdraws from race to become next UN chief

Beyond Security Council reform, Guterres used his address to warn that the world is facing four major "tests of power": war and peace, inequality, climate change and artificial intelligence.

"The faultlines in our world are widening. Cracks have become canyons," he said, pointing to conflicts and growing divisions across the world.

He also called for stronger international governance of artificial intelligence, warning that decisions involving life and death should not be handed over to machines.

His final General Assembly address comes as the UN prepares for a leadership transition, with seven candidates now in the race to succeed him.

These are Costa Rica's Rebeca Grynspan, Guyana's Carolyn Rodrigues Birkett, Ecuador's María Fernanda Espinosa and Ivonne A-Baki alongside Argentina's Rafael Grossi, Uganda's Olara Otunnu and Senegal's Macky Sall.

The race has particular significance for gender representation, as no woman has ever served as UN secretary-general in the organisation's more than 80-year history.

World.title: Michigan student confronts El-Sayed over Iran stance in tense exchange: ‘Do you stand with us?’
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

A Michigan student confronted Democratic U.S. Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed about his position on Iran during a town hall Wednesday, invoking his family's stated persecution by the Iranian regime before repeatedly pressing the candidate on whether he stood with Iranians opposing the government.

Iman Dashti, who identified himself as Persian, told El-Sayed during a town hall at the University of Michigan that members of his family had suffered under Iran's government.

"My cousin was hunted in the streets of Iran by the IRGC because her hijab wasn't on right," Dashti said. He also alleged that her uncle was sentenced to death and received 50 lashes under the Iranian government.

ABDUL EL-SAYED PROTESTED AGAINST 'EX-TERRORISTS' WHO CONVERTED TO CHRISTIANITY, UNEARTHED REPORT REVEALS

Dashti then confronted El-Sayed over leaked audio from earlier this year in which he said he did not want to comment on the death of former Iranian Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei because "there are a lot of people in Dearborn who are sad today."

"That silence had a gaping hole in our community," Dashti told El-Sayed Wednesday.

Dashti asked El-Sayed whether he regretted that silence, whether he would renounce people who held vigils supporting Khamenei and whether he stood "unequivocally against the IRGC" and the Islamic Republic of Iran.

El-Sayed responded by arguing that the United States has too often acted as "the world's policeman" while saying he supported movements for democracy and freedom abroad.

AFTER 6 MONTHS OF WAR, US MUST PREPARE FOR A FUTURE AFTER IRAN’S GOVERNMENT FALLS

"One can disagree with the governance of a foreign country. One can stand in solidarity with freedom and democracy movements," El-Sayed said.

He went on to reject U.S.-led regime change in Iran.

"I will always stand for and with democratic movements always," El-Sayed said. "But I also don't believe that we were in the right to go to war to topple the government of Iran. It was not our responsibility to do. It is the responsibility of the people of Iran to decide what their leadership should look like."

Dashti pressed him again.

"You stand with us?" he asked.

"I will always stand with movements for freedom and democracy," El-Sayed responded, before again warning against U.S. involvement in regime change.

"We should not be in the business of regime change," he said.

El-Sayed added moments later, "I want freedom and democracy for the people of Iran, no question. But I want that to be done by the people of Iran, coming together as a community to decide how to create democratic change in their society."

Fox News Digital reached out to El-Sayed's campaign for additional comment on the exchange and attempted to reach Dashti through Instagram.

El-Sayed, who won Michigan's Democratic Senate primary in August, is running against Republican former Rep. Mike Rogers for the seat being vacated by retiring Democratic Sen. Gary Peters. The contest has drawn substantial national attention and spending.

The Iran confrontation was one of several notable exchanges during Wednesday's "Students vs. Billionaires" town hall at El-Sayed's alma mater.

KAMALA HARRIS BACKS MAJOR CHANGES TO THE SUPREME COURT, ELECTORAL COLLEGE AHEAD OF POSSIBLE 2028 CAMPAIGN

While discussing public health infrastructure, El-Sayed appeared to make a prediction about the party and the gender that will win the White House in 2028.

"I'm looking forward to working with the next Democratic president when she takes office in 2029," El-Sayed said, adding that he hoped to work with that administration to modernize the nation's public health infrastructure.

El-Sayed did not identify whom he had in mind.

His remarks came as former Vice President Kamala Harris, the 2024 Democrat presidential nominee, returned to Michigan to campaign with El-Sayed. Harris has not announced a 2028 presidential campaign.

El-Sayed also criticized President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance during the event.

"Donald Trump and JD Vance can't seem to keep my name out their mouth," El-Sayed said. "They don't really know how to say it, though, which is fine, because I believe in teaching opportunities."

Trump and other national Republicans have repeatedly targeted El-Sayed during the midterm campaign, while El-Sayed has responded by criticizing the president.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"As he noted in his response, Abdul will always stand with movements for freedom and democracy, and he condemns government anti-free speech violence," Roxie Richner, El-Sayed's campaign spokesperson, said in a statement to Fox News Digital.

"Abdul has also been clear that the United States should not be in the business of spending our tax dollars abroad on regime change wars that take our service members’ lives, waste our tax dollars and raise our prices. He believes American taxpayer dollars are best spent here at home to invest in infrastructure, education and healthcare."

World.title: NYC kitten rescue defends ‘NO F---ING MAGA’ adoption policy as PETA calls for it to be abolished
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

After posting an explicit warning that MAGA supporters, conservatives and apolitical applicants need not apply, a New York City kitten rescue is defending its screening process against mounting criticism, including from PETA, which called on the group to scrap the ideological ban.

"Homeless animals don’t care which side of abortion you are on or whether you believe in global warming or support Palestine or Israel or if you don’t vote at all, ever. They care if you love them and will give them a good home," PETA founder Ingrid Newkirk told Fox News Digital.

"We hope this policy, which is humancentric, is reconsidered and abolished."

The dispute centers on Itty Bitty City Kitties, a Rockaway Beach-based rescue that describes itself as a 501(c)(3) nonprofit specializing in orphaned and neonatal kittens, feral cat welfare and adoptions. The organization is also listed among New York state’s registered pet rescues.

ONE OF NATION'S LARGEST CHRISTIAN FOSTER AGENCIES WILL NOT ALLOW LGBTQ COUPLES TO ADOPT CHILDREN

In a social media post reviewed by Fox News Digital, the rescue laid out a series of political positions it said could disqualify prospective adopters.

"MAGA? Nope."

"Conservative? Nope."

"‘I’m not political’? Nice loophole. Still nope."

An accompanying image of a kitten bore the message, "NO. F---ING. MAGA."

The post drew wider attention after Libs of TikTok posted it on X, prompting questions about whether the language represented the rescue’s actual adoption practices.

Fox News Digital contacted Itty Bitty City Kitties and asked whether an applicant could be rejected for identifying as MAGA, conservative or apolitical.

Samantha Knox, who has publicly identified herself as the director of Itty Bitty City Kitties, defended the organization’s screening approach by saying its overriding responsibility is the welfare of the animals in its care.

"As an animal welfare rescue, our primary responsibility is ensuring the animals in our care go to safe, compassionate homes," Knox told Fox News Digital.

She said the organization considers "public conduct and demonstrated values" and argued that a record of "celebrat[ing] cruelty" can raise concerns about an applicant’s suitability to care for an animal.

"A history of celebrating harm or abuse, be it toward people or animals, is one of the biggest red flags in animal rescue," Knox said. "We stand by our mission and will never place a vulnerable animal with anyone, ever, who we feel is a danger to the welfare of the animal."

OREGON SETTLES WITH CHRISTIAN MOTHER DENIED FOSTER CARE ADOPTION OVER GENDER IDENTITY BELIEFS

Fox News Digital followed up with a narrower question, asking whether a person who identifies as MAGA or conservative, but has no documented history of animal cruelty, threats, neglect or violence, would be eligible to adopt.

"Itty Bitty City Kitties does not screen or reject applicants based on registered political party affiliation," Knox responded. "MAGA is a political movement and ideology, not a recognized political party."

Knox said adoption evaluations instead concern "conduct, ethical alignment and animal safety."

"We reserve the right to reject any application where an applicant’s expressed values, public statements or actions demonstrate a failure to meet our safety and welfare standards," she said.

NEW JERSEY POLICE PULL OUT 3-FOOT PYTHON FROM WOMAN'S CAR GRILLE, BODYCAM VIDEO SHOWS

Asked again whether a MAGA or conservative applicant without a history of cruelty, threats, neglect or violence could adopt from the organization, Knox did not provide a yes-or-no answer.

"Media-driven requests to force complex animal welfare evaluations into a binary ‘yes or no’ premise fundamentally misrepresent how responsible adoption screenings operate," she said.

Knox added that "active support for or alignment with social movements" the rescue believes normalizes or promotes cruelty can be treated as "actionable conduct" and said adoption decisions are made "holistically under these welfare and safety standards."

Knox also provided Fox News Digital with screenshots she said showed explicit, hostile messages directed at the rescue after its political posts.

Knox said messages of that nature illustrated the kind of conduct the rescue considers relevant when evaluating prospective homes. PETA, however, drew a different line.

"Political affiliation is not a reliable measure of whether someone will be a good guardian," the organization told Fox News Digital, adding that a person's actions and statements, along with demonstrated treatment of people and animals, can be relevant to an adoption decision.

PETA said rescues should focus on "objective animal welfare factors," including an applicant’s history of animal care, ability to meet an animal’s needs and evidence of cruelty, neglect or violence.

"Shelters and rescues exist to protect animals, not to serve as political gatekeepers," PETA said.

Itty Bitty City Kitties’ public adoption page describes what the organization calls a "Fully Supported Adoption Model," under which prospective owners submit an application, references, employment and living information, participate in a phone interview and complete a FaceTime or Zoom interview in lieu of a home visit.

The rescue’s published "MUST LIST" says adopters must keep animals up to date on veterinary care; keep them indoors or leashed outside; never declaw them; maintain a plan for travel, illness or death; not simply give away an animal they can no longer care for; and be financially able to provide for its welfare.

The public-facing requirements reviewed by Fox News Digital do not mention MAGA, conservatism, political affiliation or political ideology.

The organization has also used its social media account for other political messaging.

On Sept. 10, Itty Bitty City Kitties posted an image of a kitten carrying the words, "Kittens. Don’t. Mourn. Nazis."

"For absolutely no reason at all on this day one year later..." text on the image stated.

"Just a little kitten making sure we all know where we stand," the accompanying caption read, followed by hashtags including "#kitten," "#cat," "#politics" and "#iykyk."

While the post did not name late conservative activist Charlie Kirk, it was published exactly one year after his assassination at Utah Valley University on Sept. 10, 2025.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Knox also invoked the rescue’s nonprofit status in defending its ability to take positions on political and social issues, saying 501(c)(3) organizations are permitted to maintain issue-based standards aligned with their missions as long as they do not engage in partisan political campaigning.

PETA, while objecting to the use of political affiliation as a measure of adoption suitability, said an applicant’s actual behavior toward animals can, and should, matter regardless of ideology.

"More broadly, anyone who condones, celebrates or participates in harming animals demonstrates a troubling lack of empathy," PETA said.

World.title: English soccer star Harry Kane wants to play in the MLS and kick in the NFL at the same time
World.content:
We don't see enough two-sport athletes these days. It's such a cool phenomenon that we haven't really seen in a while.

However, English soccer star Harry Kane wouldn't mind taking a crack at it.

Because if he winds up in the MLS, he wouldn't mind spending his free time on an NFL roster.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

ENGLISH SOCCER STAR HARRY KANE CALLS ROUND OF GOLF WITH TRUMP A ‘SURREAL EXPERIENCE’

According to The Athletic, Kane was recently quoted as saying that he was close to re-upping with the Bundesliga's Bayern Munich. That led to a question about his plans beyond this next deal.

One of those plans was something he has reportedly talked about multiple times over the years, and that was switching sports.

He's talked about golfing professionally, but this time he was focused on trading football for American football.

"That is something I will try and look at a bit more seriously," he said. "It all depends on what happens in my career over the next five or six years, the motivation and what I want to do. The NFL is a lot more realistic than the golf one, let’s put it that way."

But what had never come up before was the idea of Kane winding down his career stateside in the MLS while also moonlighting as a placekicker.

SOMEONE NEEDS TO STEP IN AND DEFEND CODY RHODES' AWFUL, TERRIBLE PLACEKICKING PERFORMANCE

"Maybe if I am in the MLS in the future or somewhere like that it might be a thing where you could connect the two, with the seasons," he said. "But it is in the back of my mind because right now, I am feeling that I want to play as long as I can here."

Nice save at the end. The team about to re-sign you probably doesn't want to hear about your plans to play in the MLS and kick extra points on the side.

But do you know who does want to hear that? The rest of us.

That would just be a fun thing to watch, and Kane obviously has the leg to boot a pigskin quite a long way if he can nail down those pesky mechanics.

Which it looks like he may have already done.

At least a few teams are probably setting reminders to see what Kane is up to when his Bayern Munich deal is up.

World.title: Trump likely ‘smirked’ as 'crass' Iranian president lashed out at US in UN speech: expert
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian’s sharp rebuke of Washington at the United Nations would have drawn little more than a "smirk" from President Donald Trump, who knows he "holds the cards," a foreign policy expert told Fox News Digital Wednesday.

The assessment came after Pezeshkian and Trump addressed the U.N. General Assembly in New York from the same podium within 24 hours of one another, trading sharp rhetoric as tensions between Washington and Tehran continue to mount.

"Trump understands he holds the cards, and he may not even have paid much attention to what the Iranian president was saying," Behnam Ben Taleblu, a senior fellow at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies (FDD), told Fox News Digital.

Pezeshkian accused the United States and Israel of attacking Iran while portraying his country as the victim of aggression.

THE TOP MOMENTS FROM IRAN PRESIDENT’S TENSE VISIT TO US SOIL AS WAR RAGES

"We have only defended ourselves. We are not terrorists," Pezeshkian claimed.

"Our innocent people have been the targets of cowardly attacks and aggressions imposed upon our country. America and Israel attacked us."

"I’m sure that would have drawn a smirk or a smile or a chuckle from the president’s face, seeing that crassness," Taleblu said, pointing to what he described as a sharp contrast between Pezeshkian’s rhetoric and the Iranian government’s track record.

Pezeshkian’s address came after Trump used the same U.N. stage to defend the U.S. conflict with Iran and warn that Tehran faces a stark choice between reaching a deal and facing further destruction.

"Or do I annihilate the Islamic Republic, and do it quickly, never giving them a chance to kill and destroy people and countries again?" Trump said on Tuesday.

While the rhetoric from both leaders was pointed, Taleblu said their broader diplomatic positions remain largely predictable.

TRUMP TO ZERO-IN ON IRAN NUCLEAR THREAT, GAZA PLAN AND UN OVERHAUL IN WORLD STAGE SPEECH

"To a certain degree, both President Trump and President Pezeshkian’s speeches before the U.N. General Assembly’s 81st session were predictable," Taleblu said.

"Predictable because the status of both countries and their foreign policy toward the other are in a fairly predictable pattern right now."

Despite the threats and recriminations, the two adversaries also appear to be still testing a diplomatic path behind the scenes.

Trump said Tuesday that U.S. special envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner spoke with Iranian officials for roughly three hours on the sidelines of the General Assembly and characterized the discussions as productive.

Witkoff later said the talks were conducted through mediators who shuttled between the U.S. and Iranian delegations.

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi also represented Tehran in the discussions, according to reports.

KUSHNER TOUTS UNPRECEDENTED IRAN CONTACTS AS TEHRAN DENIES TRUMP BACKCHANNEL

Both sides, Taleblu said, are attempting "to make time a weapon on their side" and "to put the burden of choosing between escalation and engagement on the other."

But Taleblu went on to characterize Pezeshkian’s broader message as an attempt to cast Iran as a victim through an anti-American, anti-Israel and anti-imperialist framework.

"It seemed to be more of a global South, anti-American, anti-Israeli, kind of anti-colonial, anti-imperialist message that he was looking to kind of paint the Islamic Republic as the victim," Taleblu said.

"In reality, the long-serving victim in this entire crisis is the Iranian people because of the policies of the Islamic Republic."

The competing messages — confrontation from the U.N. podium and diplomacy behind the scenes — highlighted the unresolved tensions between Washington and Tehran as officials explore whether negotiations can produce an off-ramp from the conflict.

TRUMP KEEPS FORECASTING AN IRAN DEAL — WHY THE WHITE HOUSE STILL THINKS IT CAN HAPPEN

"Despite the tough talk at the podium, both sides still feel like they need to signal an interest in talks, even though they’re both trying to use talks to shape an outcome that is more conducive to their interests," Taleblu said.

Pezeshkian also told the General Assembly that Tehran would not surrender to military pressure while signaling that Iran remained open to diplomacy.

"I think the Iranians are trying to signal an interest in talks, but they may run into a brick wall quite soon if they foot-drag or delay or don’t meaningfully provide any kind of substantive change in their policy," Taleblu said, citing Iran’s positions on the Persian Gulf, the Strait of Hormuz and its nuclear program.

"Ultimately, if the positions remain the same, the fact that they’re oscillating between shooting and talking doesn’t mean much because the red lines haven’t actually moved.

"Of course, the Trump administration is looking for a political win here."

World.title: Tylenol murders mystery deepens after sheriff’s office solves decades-old ‘Unknown Wanderer’ cold case
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

A mysterious man who died of cyanide poisoning inside an Idaho church more than four decades ago has finally been identified, and investigators say his past raises questions about a possible connection to the still-unsolved 1982 Chicago Tylenol murders.

The man known for decades as the "Unknown Wanderer" was Dr. Mathew Francis Betkouski, an organic chemist with a history of discussing cyanide and poison, the Ada County Sheriff's Office in Boise announced Wednesday.

Investigators said they couldn't place Betkouski in Chicago during the final week of September 1982, when seven people died after taking Tylenol capsules laced with cyanide, and they are not naming him as a suspect.

TYLENOL MURDERS SUSPECT GAVE EERIE FINAL INTERVIEW BEFORE DEATH

Dr. Park Dietz, a forensic psychiatrist who was consulted during the original Tylenol investigation and reviewed the evidence gathered on Betkouski, offered a stronger assessment.

"It's an extraordinary thing to have been around at the beginning in 1982, and now today in 2026, to see very likely closure," Dietz said.

Dietz said groups of forensic psychiatrists, psychologists and criminal profilers who were anonymously presented with information about Betkouski overwhelmingly considered him a viable suspect.

Betkouski died on Dec. 4, 1982, after walking into Sacred Heart Catholic Church in Boise. Authorities determined he died from cyanide poisoning, but he carried no identification, and his fingerprints produced no match.

REMAINS FOUND IN UTAH DESERT 28 YEARS AGO WITH HELP OF A PSYCHIC FINALLY IDENTIFIED THROUGH DNA GENEALOGY

The mystery endured for decades until investigators traced one of nearly 30 keys found on him to Jacksonville, Florida, where Betkouski had lived. DNA recovered from his wallet and later compared with a sample from his brother helped establish his identity.

Investigators subsequently uncovered several details that drew their attention to the Tylenol case.

A former colleague recalled Betkouski discussing the "perfect crime" and cyanide, while another scientist recalled him saying poison could be introduced into over-the-counter capsules, according to investigators.

Authorities also found a map of Chicago and a bottle of sodium cyanide among belongings kept at his family's Los Angeles home. Investigators stressed that the poison was not the potassium cyanide used in the Tylenol murders.

THE TYLENOL MURDERS: A LOOK BACK AT THE RASH OF 1982 DRUG STORE POISONINGS

Photos showed Betkouski had visited Chicago, but investigators determined they were likely taken in December 1981 and said they cannot establish that he returned when the Tylenol poisonings occurred.

Betkouski disappeared from his New Mexico home on Oct. 15, 1982, and turned up dead in Boise seven weeks later after apparently changing his appearance.

Authorities have turned their findings over to investigators in the Chicago area and are seeking information about Betkouski's movements and communications in 1982.

"This isn't over," Ada County Sheriff Matt Clifford said.

World.title: Blue Jays' Vladimir Guerrero Jr. says his $500M contract was for past performance – not future results
World.content:
Vladimir Guerrero Jr. has four games left before he can put his 2026 Toronto Blue Jays season behind him.

Guerrero, the six-time All-Star who signed the third highest-paid extension in MLB history in April 2025 at $500 million, has hit just nine home runs and slugged .359 to date for a career-low .695 OPS to date.

The Blue Jays, winners of the American League pennant this past season, where Guerrero was a major factor in reaching the World Series, were mathematically eliminated from this year’s postseason race as they hold a 77-81 record entering Wednesday.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

For a player that is worth so much, especially financially, to an organization’s success, Guerrero’s down year has led to some vitriol from the Blue Jays’ fan base. And that’s likely to continue after hearing recent comments from the star infielder.

Guerrero, 27, sat down with Telemicro News recently, where he discussed his struggles at the plate this season, and how it reflects on his contract extension.

His comments were, well, interesting.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

"The contract I got was based on what I did, not necessarily for what I’m going to do," Guerrero said, as translated by MLB reporter Héctor Gómez. "I understand why the fans believe it’s the other way around. Sometimes, I think that way, too, like, ‘Oh, they give me this money, and I’m not doing enough,’ but you know I try my best, and I’m working hard.

"The fans, I know how they are, when you are doing great they are 100% behind you. But when you are not at your best, not everybody is behind you, almost nobody supports you. Those are my real fans, the ones that are supporting me all the time."

After catching heat from Blue Jays fans, Guerrero was approached about the viral quotes, which he responded to.

"That was a quote from the interview when she asked me how I felt about this year," Guerrero said, via MLB.com. "I said that, obviously, I feel really bad about the year that I had, that I couldn’t help my team get to the postseason. I said I felt – that it’s my personal opinion – that every player gets paid for what they have done. With that said, you guys have got to remember that I signed my contract at the beginning of last year, then I did put up a good year. Then, the kind of playoffs that I had to help the team get into the World Series.

"To the fans, I’ve never stopped working very hard. I am going to go into the offseason again to prepare myself the best I can. Physically, mentally, everything that I have like I always do for my team and my teammates."

In Guerrero’s defense, that is technically what the Blue Jays did when they dished out his 14-year, $500 million extension, which is only behind Shohei Ohtani’s 10-year, $700 million deal with the Los Angeles Dodgers and Juan Soto’s 15-year, $765 million deal with the New York Mets. The franchise paid Guerrero for what he did from his debut in 2019 up to a fantastic 2025 campaign, where he belted eight homers and hit .397 across 18 postseason games.

But these comments show that Guerrero mustn’t be aware of what putting pen to money-filled paper meant in April 2025. No longer is it time in any sport, let alone Major League Baseball, where contracts are dished out based solely on past performance. It’s looking ahead to the future, where those past performances are expected to continue through a much-more lucrative deal.

MLB franchises sign players to contracts based on the market, and that market is justified by how the player will perform for them later on, while obviously looking at the track record in the past.

With any investment, those dishing out the big bucks want a return.

So, in a season where the home run total for a slugger is less than double digits – he still has time to at least get to 10 – and a career-low WAR (albeit the 2020 COVID-shortened campaign) has been accumulated, the Blue Jays and its fan base have every right to be disappointed. Yes, Guerrero was a major reason why Toronto reached the World Series in 2025, but the team and its fans are also allowed to voice displeasure with not just a down year – a career-worst performance in various metrics.

Would the Mets have dished out the highest-paying contract in league history if they didn’t expect Soto to continue performing at his superstar pace? No.

Would the Dodgers have agreed to give Ohtani $700 million, with heavy deferrals, might we add, to pay him for years without helping them reach their World Series goals? No.

OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD

From Mike Trout, to Mookie Betts, to Aaron Judge and the list goes on, every franchise wants to see a player they sign, especially for nine figures, to pay dividends. That’s the reality of the situation, whether Guerrero wants to view his deal as what he’s done in the past.

This is just one season, but Guerrero’s outlook needs to change just as much as his production moving forward on the remaining 13 years of his deal.

World.title: Just one small serving of ultra-processed food a day linked to higher disease risk, major study finds
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

Just an extra 3½ ounces of ultra-processed foods (UPFs) a day was linked to a higher risk of chronic disease, according to a new large-scale analysis.

The study, published Sept. 22 in the journal Family Medicine and Community Health, looked at nearly 8.8 million adults who participated in studies across the Americas, Europe, Asia and Oceania, with follow-up periods ranging from two to 32 years.

For every additional 100 grams of UPFs consumed daily, researchers found an association with a 14% higher risk of cardiovascular events, a 4% higher risk of cancer, a 3% higher risk of death from any cause and a 2% higher risk of metabolic syndrome or diabetes, according to a news release.

BRINGING THIS POPULAR DRINK TO A JOB INTERVIEW COULD HURT YOUR CHANCES, EXPERTS WARN

UPFs are typically packaged and convenient, made through extensive industrial processing and often packed with additives. They can include sugary drinks, processed meats, packaged snacks and candy.

One hundred grams is about the size of a 3½-ounce bag of corn chips, a small box of candy or a single-serve cup of mini cookies.

People with the highest intake of UPFs also had higher risks of digestive diseases, depression or anxiety, obesity, cancer and cardiovascular events than those with the lowest intake of the foods.

5 ULTRA-PROCESSED FOODS THAT MAY BE WORSE FOR YOUR HEALTH THAN YOU THINK, EXPERT SAYS

"Given that UPF-related chronic diseases often cluster as multimorbidity, reducing consumption of UPFs and replacing them with minimally processed alternatives may be relevant for chronic disease prevention and primary care management," wrote the researchers, led by Xiao Liu, a cardiologist at Sun Yat-sen Memorial Hospital in China and a research fellow at Duke-NUS Medical School in Singapore.

"A diet built around whole, minimally processed foods is one of the best investments we can make in our long-term health."

These types of foods tend to crowd out healthier, nutrient-dense options, according to Kelly Springer, a New York-based registered dietitian and founder of Kelly's Choice.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"It's not that you can never eat them again," Springer, who was not involved in the research, told Fox News Digital. "It's the fact that we are not getting real foods — real foods like fruits, vegetables, beans, nuts, whole grains."

Rather than focusing on taking foods away, Springer recommended adding protein and fiber to meals and snacks. She suggested options such as an apple with peanut butter, nuts with cucumbers or meals built around beans, chicken or tuna alongside fruits, vegetables and whole grains.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

"A diet built around whole, minimally processed foods is one of the best investments we can make in our long-term health," she added.

Springer noted that the study was observational, so it cannot establish that UPFs directly caused the poor health outcomes.

CLICK HERE TO 

It also relied on participants' self-reported diets and may not be able to account for other lifestyle factors.

Nonetheless, the study can teach people about the link between ultra-processed foods and chronic disease, Springer said.

"Home Improvement" star Jonathan Taylor Thomas was detained after reportedly resisting an officer in Westlake Village, California, Monday.

According to court records obtained by Fox News Digital, Thomas was detained at the Malibu/Lost Hills sheriff's station. After being booked, Thomas was released.

Law enforcement sources told TMZ the child actor was a passenger in a vehicle that was stopped by police. The outlet reported that deputies told Thomas to stay inside the vehicle, but he allegedly exited anyway. Thomas was also reportedly drunk at the time of the incident.

‘HOME IMPROVEMENT’ STAR JONATHAN TAYLOR THOMAS MAKES RARE APPEARANCE IN REUNION PHOTO WITH CO-STARS

In July, Richardson sparked a wave of nostalgia when she shared a rare reunion photo with her former "Home Improvement" sons, Thomas and Smith, more than 25 years after the beloved sitcom ended.

"My other boys," Richardson captioned the snapshot with a heart emoji.

The reunion offered fans a rare glimpse of Thomas, who largely stepped away from Hollywood after becoming one of the biggest child stars of the 1990s.

But at the height of his fame, Thomas made a surprising decision to walk away.

World.title: U.S. and China agree to extend trade truce through Jan. 10, Bessent says
World.content:
The United States and China have agreed to extend a bilateral trade truce that was set to expire in November through Jan. 10, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Wednesday.

The announcement came after Bessent and China’s vice premier, He Lifeng, held an unscheduled meeting in Washington.

“We will extend what we call the ‘Busan Agreement’ — the economic détente between the two countries that was scheduled to end on Nov. 10 — that is going to be extended until Jan. 10,” Bessent said in an interview on Fox News Channel.

Bessent said it’s possible a larger economic package will be agreed upon by January. But it’s also possible to “just roll the current deal” and extend it further.

“There are some deliverables that have not been perfect on the Chinese side, so we also want to see, now that we’ve sat down and told them our expectations, if over the coming months they can be more fulsome in enacting the agreement,” he said.

The announcement, a big win for economic stability in both countries, came only minutes after Chinese President Xi Jinping touched down to begin a multiday state visit to Washington.

Bessent also indicated that there could be further announcements in coming days from the Chinese delegation, including agreements to buy more American agricultural products and potential deals in the financial services sector.

Since Sunday, Bessent and U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer have been holding talks with their Chinese counterparts to lay the groundwork for the closely watched state visit.

On Sunday, Bessent and Greer announced that the U.S. and China had proposed exchanging alerts about AI-related hacking incidents, especially those that concern national security.

The U.S. and China could also agree on lists of goods on which lower tariffs would be applied as part of President Donald Trump’s “Board of Trade” initiative with China, Greer told reporters.

“We expect that the types of goods you’ll see in those lists are consumer goods, low-tech items coming in from the Chinese side,” he said. “On the U.S. side, energy products, agricultural goods, potentially medical devices and other things like that.”

Xi’s visit is his first trip to the U.S. in more than a decade.

News of the trade truce extension is likely to be widely welcomed in Washington and Beijing, given that the U.S. and China are vital sources of goods for each other and for their millions of consumers and businesses.
